dated_statement: The Baloch, speaking a Northwest Iranian language, arrived from the northwest in what is now southeastern Iran and western Pakistan in waves between 1000 and 1500 AD.
date_range: 1000-1500 AD, explicitly described as waves rather than an event
which_of_the_four_histories: LANGUAGE HISTORY, and speaker movement, asserted together. The statement does not separate the arrival of the language from the arrival of its speakers.
evidence_basis_stated: None given in the retrieved text.
hedge_in_the_source: 'are generally thought to have arrived'. The author reports a field consensus and does not assert it in his own voice.
locator: Spooner, Balochi: Towards a Biography of the Language, 2012, abstract as returned by SRC-053
upstream_dependency: Not traceable from an abstract. The consensus it reports is presumably the one Korn 2005 and Elfenbein document; neither was read, so this cannot be checked for circularity.
notes: The one linguist-authored date frame reached in this session, and the answer to the owner's probe. Its width is the finding: a 500-year window reported as consensus is not a date, and this unit does not narrow it.

dated_statement: In the fifteenth century the Rind and Lashar tribes, with many other Baloch tribes, migrated from western Makran, conquering other Baloch tribes on the way, and formed the first unified Baloch confederacy. Mir Chakar Khan Rind ruled from Sibi from 1487 to 1511.
date_range: 15th century for the migration; 1487-1511 for the reign
which_of_the_four_histories: POLITICAL AND TRIBAL IDENTITY. Not language history. A confederacy forming in the fifteenth century says nothing on its own about when Balochi began to be spoken in the area it covered.
evidence_basis_stated: Baloch historiography and epic tradition; the regnal dates are attributed to Harrison 1981:12 and the confederacy to Qizalbash 1979:19.
hedge_in_the_source: 'Tradition holds' is used for the naming of Balochistan; the migration and the regnal dates are stated without hedge.
locator: Badalkhan, 'Lord of the Iron Bow', Oral Tradition, 2005, first-page extract as returned by SRC-053
upstream_dependency: Harrison 1981, Qizalbash 1979, Baluch 1965, Hetu Ram 1898, Rzehak 1998 - none opened. Hetu Ram 1898 is a colonial-period compilation and its standing is not assessed here.
notes: The tightest chronology retrieved and the one most exposed to misuse, which is why its history is named on the face of the row. It falls INSIDE DMC-001's window and is therefore consistent with it, but it is a different kind of claim about a different object.

dated_statement: Balochi loanword layers show continuing influence of Persian from the earliest times to the present day; the predecessor of contemporary Balochi seems to have been a dialect rather similar to Parthian but differing from it in a number of details.
date_range: No absolute dates. 'From the earliest times' is relative; the Parthian comparison implies a Middle Iranian horizon without dating Balochi's arrival anywhere.
which_of_the_four_histories: LANGUAGE HISTORY and LOANWORD HISTORY, kept separate by the source itself: the Parthian statement is about descent, the Persian statement about contact.
evidence_basis_stated: Historical phonology across Balochi dialects, compared with New Persian, Parthian and Avestan; plus selected lexical fields.
locator: Korn, Towards a Historical Grammar of Balochi, 2005, abstract as returned by SRC-053
notes: This is the source that would date the strata, and it was not read. Its abstract establishes that the strata ARE stratified and that a Brahui relationship is among them; it supplies no boundary, no item and no direction. HOLD-005 is open on it.

dated_statement: Kurdish and Balochi show transitional behaviour between Northwest and Southwest Iranian, participating in the change *cu > s with Southwest Iranian but not in *th > h or *dz > d, and cannot be placed in the Southwest Iranian group.
date_range: Relative only. The changes are ordered against each other; no absolute date is given.
evidence_basis_stated: A hierarchical Dirichlet process model over West Iranian sound-change reflexes, with the explicit argument that irregularity is not reducible to lexical borrowing from Persian.
hedge_in_the_source: The paper describes its own conclusions as provisional resolutions.
locator: Cathcart, Dialectal Layers in West Iranian, TPS 120(1), 2022, 1-31, DOI 10.1111/1467-968X.12225, section 'West Iranian historical phonology', full-text chunks 0008 and 0019 of 35
upstream_dependency: Morgenstierne 1926/1932/1960, Henning 1963, Schwartz 2006, Skjaervo 2009, Gershevitch 1962b - cited in the retrieved passages, none opened.
notes: The only row here retrieved as full text with a resolvable DOI. It is a relative chronology, not an absolute one, and it is included because relative chronology is what the field actually has for Balochi and because it constrains what a later absolute chronology could look like.

dated_statement: Mention of the Baloch in ancient and historical literature is random, sporadic and abstract in form, context and content, and it is hard to construct a chronological history of the Baloch from ancient historical accounts.
date_range: Not a date. A statement about the documentary record from which dates would have to come.
which_of_the_four_histories: Bears on all four by limiting what any of them can be evidenced from.
evidence_basis_stated: A survey of the ancient and medieval sources by authors working within Baloch historiography.
locator: Ahmed et al., The History of Baloch and Balochistan: A Critical Appraisal, South Asian Studies, 2017, first-page extract as returned by SRC-053
upstream_dependency: Dashti 2012, Spooner 1983, Sahlins 1968, Dames 1907 - none opened.
notes: A negative chronological statement, and the frame for the other four. If the pre-modern record is this thin, then DMC-001's 500-year window is what the evidence can bear rather than a failure of precision. Typed NOT PRODUCED for the pre-modern period: the statement is that the documentation was largely never made, not that it was made and lost.

dated_statement: A group of Brahui speakers entered Sistan and Balochistan province in Iran from the Pakistan borders within the last 400 years, and about 200 years ago a group entered southern Kerman.
date_range: c. 1626-2026 and c. 1826, from oral tradition
which_of_the_four_histories: SPEAKER MOVEMENT and LANGUAGE HISTORY together, for a recent and local event.
evidence_basis_stated: Community oral literature and the accounts of named local informants.
hedge_in_the_source: Attributed to oral literature and informants rather than asserted as documented.
locator: Sheybanifard, Word Formation in Brahui Language of Rudbar-Jonub/Rudbari, Al-Burz, 2023, abstract as returned by SRC-053
notes: HOLD, not PROVISIONAL, and the reason is procedural rather than evidentiary. This is community-authored knowledge about a living community and CLAUDE.md routes it to the rights steward for consent and attribution before it enters a register; that routing has not happened, and D-041 is the request. It is entered here at HOLD so that it is on the record and so that the reason it is not being used is visible. Two substantive cautions belong with it. It is authoritative for living identity and knowledge; it is not a Bronze Age chronology and is not read as one. And it documents a WESTWARD movement out of Pakistan in the modern period, which is not evidence for a medieval eastward one - the direction and the date are both wrong for that, and DMG-2 records that it must not be counted there.
